Remaining: `ERROR (2 errors)` = `rsync-timeout` + `snapshot:sessions`, which are the same
single `codex/sessions` wedge counted twice (the watchdog error plus the snapshot failure
it causes). Not two problems. Clear `.errors.log` only after the wedge itself is fixed.

Verification trap met here: `find -newermt '-30 minutes'` silently matches nothing on BSD
find (macOS) — it wants an absolute date. Use `find -newer <reference-file>` instead. Also
remember `rsync -a` preserves source mtimes, so freshly-copied files look old; compare
*directory* mtimes or use a reference file to prove a capture ran.

Note the run ordering: Drive SNAPs run *before* the SSD capture, so a long `codex/sessions`
seed delays the SSD layer within a given run. Not a failure, just a wait.

## `snapshot:sessions` — evidence from a live reproduction, 2026-08-14 15:20 (stack-doctor)

Caught the hang in progress and narrowed it. **Root cause still open** — this section is
evidence, not a verdict. Everything below is measured, not inferred:

- **It is a hang, not a slow transfer.** Four rsync processes (client `-a ... codex/sessions/`,
  its `--server` receiver, plus two older receivers) sat at **0.01–0.03 s of CPU across
  34–85 minutes** of wall clock. Zero progress, not slow progress.
- **Nothing is left to copy.** The mirror is **256/256 files** — the previously-missing
  `2026/08/06/rollout-*.jsonl` is present. A complete mirror still hangs.
- **The mount is healthy.** A recursive `find` over the destination returned 256 files
  promptly, and `touch` inside the exact hung directory succeeded instantly. Reads *and*
  writes both work, so this is not a wedged DriveFS/FUSE mount.
- **The wedged processes ignore SIGTERM** (still alive minutes later in `S` state) — they
  are blocked inside a call that neither returns nor delivers signals.
- **Dry runs cannot see it**: `-n` completes clean, live runs hang. Another instance of the
  "`-DryRun` cannot verify a write path" trap above.

### Orphans are a symptom, not the cause

Two `rsync --server` receivers were **orphaned to PPID 1** (started 13:55 and 14:33). It is
tempting to call them the blocker; the timeline refutes it — the **10:31:54 run hung at the
identical point** (last line `SNAP skip (missing): .codex/memories`, no end line) while the
oldest surviving orphan did not exist until 13:55. `kill` on both orphans did not unblock
the live pair either.

Why they accumulate: **`daily-backup.ps1` contains no `pkill` at all** (verified by grep —
do not go looking for one). The anchored `pkill -f "^/usr/bin/rsync"` belongs to an *ad-hoc
wrapper used interactively in another session*. That pattern matches only the client, whose
`argv[0]` is the full path; the `--server` child's `argv[0]` is bare `rsync`, so
`pgrep -f "^/usr/bin/rsync"` returns the client alone. Every kill-and-retry therefore strands
one more receiver. If that wrapper is reused, match on `-x rsync` or the destination path.

### ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-14 17:00 — it is not rsync

Ran the copy in the foreground with `-avv`, unpiped. It printed ~99 lines of
`... is uptodate` and froze mid-filename. Then:

- `sample <receiver-pid>` showed the process blocked in **`__mmap`** — one frame, not moving.
- `lsof` on it showed FD 5 open on a specific **destination** file:
  `codex/sessions/2026/05/08/rollout-2026-05-08T17-14-58-019e09a8-*.jsonl`.
- **`head -c 512` on that destination file hangs by itself**, with zero rsync processes
  running. A plain read. So the file is unreadable through DriveFS.
- A 44-file sample elsewhere in the same mirror read instantly, so it is **specific files,
  not the mount**.

The files are **DriveFS placeholders** — uploaded to Google, then evicted from the local
cache. Census of the destination on 2026-08-14: 256 files, **122 materialized (48.5 MB on
disk), 134 placeholder-only (240.7 MB logical, 0 bytes local)**. Source is 256/256
materialized. Detect with `stat -f '%b %z'`: blocks==0 with a nonzero logical size means
the content is not local. Reading one forces an on-demand fetch, and that fetch stalls —
which is what blocks `__mmap`. rsync was the victim, not the cause. **Do not chase rsync
flags**; the block happens at open, before any comparison strategy applies.

**This inverts the problem: the backup is fine, the verification is what's broken.** All
256 files are on Google's servers. Nothing is missing. What fails is the *next* run's
attempt to re-read them to confirm they match. Never conclude "the snapshot is broken"
from this failure mode.

Also: `du -sh` on the destination reports the *local cache* (48 MB), not the logical 289 MB.
Both numbers are true and mean different things — do not treat the gap as missing data.

Diagnostic sequence that worked, reuse it: `sample <pid>` for the blocking syscall →
`lsof -p <pid>` for the file it is on → bounded `head -c` on that path to prove the
filesystem, not the tool, is at fault.

**Attempted fix that DID NOT WORK**: pinning `My Drive/Backups` "Available offline" via the
Finder context menu (there is no CLI or xattr for it — the app ships no control surface).
Eric pinned it 2026-08-14 17:30. Result: **one** file materialized, then flat for 5 minutes
(133 placeholders, 49.2 MB, unchanged). Restarting Drive did not help either.

**DriveFS on this Mac is itself unhealthy** — this is the real blocker, not rsync and not
the pin:
- It refused a graceful `osascript quit` for 20s and needed SIGKILL. Its log emitted
  `crashpad ... ThreadsStuck` every 6s. Restarting cleared the stuck threads but nothing else.
- The **download** queue fails, not just uploads: `merger.cc:969:ProcessDownloadEvent` +
  `HandleFailedChange [DownloadMergeQueueItem]`. DriveFS cannot pull content *down*.
- Signs of local DB damage: `item_query_handler.cc:1135:OnGetItemIds Ignoring item
  local-376561 that's missing from ...`.
- NOT quota: 671 GB used of 5.5 TB.

**Do not clear the DriveFS content cache as the remedy.** It converts every materialized
file into a placeholder needing re-download, feeding the exact mechanism that is failing —
122 readable files could become 0. If DriveFS is repaired, do it by signing out and back in
to force a DB rebuild, deliberately, with time to watch it.

### RESOLVED 2026-08-14 — the backup was never broken, the verification was

**Final mechanism**: files Drive has evicted from local cache are placeholders. Fetching a
placeholder through DriveFS is *unreliable* — usually fast, sometimes stalling for tens of
minutes. rsync blocking on such a fetch is the entire "wedge". Proof it is a slow fetch and
not a poisoned file: the file that hung four separate times **now reads instantly**, and its
blocks went 0 → 770,048 — the repeated read attempts eventually completed the fetch. Six
other placeholders read fine first try. Nothing was corrupt.

**`~/.claude/scripts/verify-drive-backup.sh` (`0d2edb5`) is now the way to verify.** It
compares the Drive API's server-side `md5Checksum` against a local md5 — metadata only, no
DriveFS read, batched ~25 names per query. First run on `~/.codex/sessions`:
**256/256 verified, 0 mismatch, 0 missing.** The snapshot that logged `FAILED` for days was
complete and byte-correct the whole time.

Do not "fix" this by deleting Drive copies. Both files that hung were verified byte-identical
to source *before* anything was touched — deleting would have destroyed a good backup to
repair a read path.

**It is plain fetch latency, scaling with file size** — no mystery left. A full read-scan of
all 256 files with a 6s per-file cap: 33 stalled, and those averaged **2,301 KB vs 1,156 KB
for the set overall** (max 15.8 MB). Bigger file, longer fetch. Nothing file-specific,
nothing corrupt. The scan itself moved the mirror from 122 → 230 materialized (48.5 → 161.8 MB
local), which is exactly what "reading materializes it" predicts.

Caution when testing this: **reading a file materializes it**, so any scan warms the cache and
a later run passes for reasons that will not hold once Drive evicts again. Timestamp results
and never treat a post-scan rsync run as a clean verification.

### Why DriveFS is unhealthy — found 2026-08-14 18:20

**Google Drive is mirroring `~/DEV` as a device-backup folder named "My Mac"**, including
**34 `.git` directories / 3,470 files**. VS Code has `"git.autofetch": true`, which rewrites
every repo's `FETCH_HEAD` on a 180s cycle; Drive uploads all 34 each time. That is the source
of the `PRECONDITION_FAILED` storms on `FETCH_HEAD` and the stuck threads in `drive_fs.txt`,
and therefore of the slow placeholder fetches upstream.

Proof (not inference): local `~/DEV/*/.git/FETCH_HEAD` all stamped 18:22:09 while Drive's

61	**Built 2026-08-31.** Closes ARMS gap 5. `~/DEV/CommandCentre/server.py`, served by
62	`com.keystone.commandcentre` (`RunAtLoad` + `KeepAlive`), own `DESIGN.md`.
63	
64	**<http://localhost:7373>** — one page answering "is anything broken?": agent
65	health, backup result, graph progress, logged failures, active projects, and
66	links to every generated report with its age.
67	
68	Design rules that must hold, each learned the hard way:
69	
70	- **Standard library only.** Python 3.14 here is PEP 668-managed, so any
71	  dependency means a venv to maintain forever. A read-only local page never
72	  earns that.
73	- **Rendered fresh per request.** Never cached, never regenerated on a timer. A
74	  page that can be stale is a page you stop believing — that is exactly why the
75	  on-demand `project-triage/dashboard.html` never became a front door.
76	- **A dashboard that contradicts the CLI is worse than no dashboard.** The file
77	  counter first used `total - len(done)` and disagreed with `gf_remaining.py` by
78	  13, because the done-list holds entries no longer in the corpus. It now does
79	  the same **set difference**, and the corpus selection is kept identical across
80	  `server.py`, `gf_gemini.py` and `gf_remaining.py`.
81	- **Judge a running service on its PID, not its last exit code.** A `KeepAlive`
82	  daemon carries the exit code of the instance that *died*, so a restart leaves a
83	  nonzero code behind permanently. `launchctl list`'s first column is the PID and
84	  the second is that stale status — reading the wrong column makes a healthy
85	  service look broken.
86	- **Live `launchctl` state is the truth**; `run-ledger.json` is shown but never
87	  allowed to claim a job succeeded. See [[keystoneos-verification-habits]].
88	- **Every source is optional** — a missing input renders "unknown", never a 500.
89	- **Bound to `127.0.0.1` only**, which is why it needs no auth. Do not change the
90	  bind address without adding one. Read-only on purpose: no buttons, so a stray
91	  browser tab cannot fire an agent. `~/.claude/scripts/skill-button.sh` exists
92	  for the day buttons are wanted.
93	
94	**The threat to a localhost service is a web page you visit, not the network.**
95	Any site your browser opens can make requests to `127.0.0.1`, so binding to
96	loopback is not a security boundary on its own. **DNS rebinding** is the real
97	attack: the attacker's domain re-resolves to `127.0.0.1`, their JavaScript
98	becomes same-origin, and it reads everything. The defence is a **`Host` header
99	allowlist** — refuse any request whose Host is not a loopback name. Three review
100	rounds were needed to get the parsing right: compare IPv6 numerically (so
101	`[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]` is recognised), refuse a second `Host` header rather than
102	guess, strip exactly one trailing DNS dot, and validate the port range. Also
103	learned: **curl silently collapses duplicate headers** — prove that guard over a
104	raw socket.
105	
106	**An allowlisted name is not an allowlisted file.** `Path.exists()` and
107	`read_bytes()` follow symlinks, so an exact-path allowlist still served
108	`/etc/hosts` when the target was swapped for a symlink. Confine the resolved
109	object too, then **read through the same descriptor you checked** (`O_NOFOLLOW`,
110	then compare the fd's `(st_dev, st_ino)` to the pre-check `lstat`) — checking a
111	path and reopening it by name is a check/use race. Close the fd in a `finally`
112	that catches every exception type, not just `OSError`.
113	
114	**Any number shown in two places must be computed by identical code.** A page
115	that contradicts the CLI destroys trust in both. Three separate counters here
116	had to be aligned four times: set difference not arithmetic, the same corpus
117	selection, the same skip gates, the same `GF_MAXBYTES` env override — including
118	its "0 means no cap" convention — and the gate applied to a progress line's
119	numerator *and* denominator.
120	
121	**Creating any new `~/DEV/<folder>` breaks the backup immediately** — the manifest
122	is default-deny, so `daily-backup` exits 1 until the folder is added to
123	`~/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json`. Working as designed; just add the entry
124	in the same turn. The `class` field answers *who keeps this when you leave
125	Baylor* — `institutional` also copies to Baylor OneDrive ("lost when Baylor
126	access ends"), `personal` stays yours. See [[backup-sync-system]].
127	
128	## The `/os` view — added 2026-09-01
129	
130	A second face over the same sources: **<http://localhost:7373/os>** (page:
131	`CommandCentre/os.html`, data: `/api/state.json`). `/` is unchanged. Renders
132	routines, 148 skills, an artifact ring, Second Brain counts, health and projects.
133	Rationale lives in `DESIGN.md` → "The `/os` view". Backup: `server.py.bak-2026-09-01`.
134	Design study it came from (video frames + original spec): `CommandCentre/reference/rubric-agentic-os/`.
135	
136	- **It is read-only, and that is not a gap to fill casually.** It shows which model
137	  and effort a skill *would* run at; it cannot run one. Run buttons and the model ×
138	  effort matrix were deliberately **not rendered** — dead controls are worse than
139	  none. `~/.claude/scripts/skill-button.sh` is the guarded write path for that day.
140	- **Never add a CORS header to `/api/state.json`, and never open `/os` as
141	  `file://`.** Same-origin is the only thing keeping the whole state object away
142	  from any site the browser has open. A `file://` page would need CORS to fetch it
143	  — that is the trap, not the fix.
144	- **`/open` allowlists ring files by identical string, recomputed per click** —
145	  same rule as `LINKS`, never a prefix or subtree test. The ring moves as files are
146	  written, so a click can 404 when it shifted underneath. That is the correct
147	  failure; widening the check is how a traversal gets in.
148	- **The ring must stay capped per folder and per project** (`RING_PER_DIR=2`,
149	  `RING_PER_PROJECT=6`). Uncapped "40 most recent" gave 22 of 40 from a single
150	  06:34 generated batch and buried every real deliverable. Verified: capped = 13
151	  projects.
152	- **`RING_EXCLUDE` keeps `COG_S2_Position_Reports` off the ring** — those filenames
153	  carry athlete names and the ring renders filenames as labels, so a glance would
154	  put named cognitive results on screen. Excluded from this view only.
155	  See [[s2-cognition-analysis]].
156	- **`SENSITIVE_PATHS` is module-level now**, shared by `src_graph` and the ring, so
157	  the graph count and the ring can never disagree about what is off-limits. Still
158	  must match `gf_gemini.py`.
159	- **Calendar and email cannot be on this page.** Both live behind MCP servers that
160	  only exist inside a Claude session; a background HTTP server cannot reach them.
161	  Caching them would break the never-stale rule the page is built on. They became
162	  System Health and Projects instead.
163	- `launchctl kickstart -k` leaves **exit `-15`** on the previous instance. Expected —
164	  judge it on the live PID, which `src_agents` already does.
165	
166	- **To verify `/os` renders, use headless Chrome — not the claude-in-chrome
167	  extension.** The extension returns `Frame with ID 0 is showing error page` for
168	  `localhost:7373` on both `localhost` and `127.0.0.1`, while `curl` gets 200 and
169	  the server logs nothing. That is the extension's site-permission gate, **not** a
170	  server fault — do not go hunting for an IPv4/IPv6 bind bug (the server is
171	  IPv4-only by design, `server.py:878`, and that is not the cause). Working check:
172	  `"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless \
173	  --disable-gpu --virtual-time-budget=6000 --screenshot=<out>.png \
174	  --window-size=1440,900 http://127.0.0.1:7373/os`
175	  **`--virtual-time-budget` is required** — without it the shot fires before the
176	  `/api/state.json` fetch resolves and every panel reads `LOADING`, which looks
177	  exactly like a broken board.

191	
192	**Current state (2026-09-03).** Two backup runs happen on most days, and the 09-02 entry was
193	right about that — but **not** because reconcile hard-codes the backup. The real mechanism,
194	traced 09-03:
195	
196	`keystone-reconcile.ps1` is a **generic make-up engine**. It has no mention of `daily-backup` at
197	all; it loops the registry at `DEV/KeystoneOS/data/jobs.json` and calls
198	`run-job.ps1 -Job <id> -Trigger reconcile -MadeUp` for any job with no success recorded today.
199	The `daily-backup` job is in that registry with `reconcile: true`, `graceMinutes: 60`,
200	`maxAttemptsPerDay: 2`, and `makeupWindow: 07:00-20:00`. Its `successProbe` greps today's
201	`daily-backup.log` for `daily-backup end: OK`. So:
202	
203	- **If no successful run is recorded by 07:00, reconcile replays it** → the ~07:00-07:10 run.
204	- **launchd `com.keystone.dailybackup` fires at 09:00 regardless** → the second run.
205	- **Run the backup by hand before 07:00 and reconcile skips it** ("already succeeded today").
206	  Confirmed 09-03: a 06:15 manual run logged `OK` at 06:25, and no 07:00 run happened.
207	
208	Registry inconsistency worth knowing: `jobs.json` records `schedule.at: "00:30"` while the live
209	plist fires at 09:00. The make-up window is what actually drives the 07:00 replay, so the stale
210	`at` has not bitten yet. Still true: `launchctl ... runs = 0` proves nothing — read the log.
211	Receipts cluster only on days CRASHBOX is attached: a mount gap, not a schedule gap.
212	
213	**"Scheduled runs cannot push" is NOT yet established — and the two contexts differ.** On
214	2026-09-03 the **09:00 launchd** run pushed `global-memory` cleanly and ended `OK (0 errors)`:
215	no `PUSH FAILED`, no `PUSH ERR`. But the **reconcile/`run-job.ps1`** context — which is where the
216	09-02 07:08 and 08-13 07:00 failures happened — **was not exercised that day**, because the manual
217	06:15 run pre-empted the replay. Do not read 09-03 as clearing the gap; it only clears launchd.
218	`daily-backup.ps1:74` no longer swallows the reason: the `Out-Null` was replaced 09-03 with
219	captured output that logs `REPO <name> : PUSH ERR | <text>` on failure only. **The error text will
220	only appear on a day nobody runs the backup by hand before 07:00.** Diagnose from that line rather
221	than assuming a credential gap. `daily-backup.err` is stale (last written 2026-08-06); never read
222	it as current. Manual remedy after a failed push is still `git -C <repo> push origin main` for
223	SecondBrain, `.claude/global-memory`, `.claude`.
224	
225	**SSD layout:** non-repo DEV dirs land in `DEV-nonrepo/`, **not** `DEV/` — there is no `DEV/`
226	on CRASHBOX (roots are `DEV-nonrepo/`, `DEV-repo-data/`, `DEV-working-tree/`, `claude/`,
227	`codex/`, `gemini/`, `SecondBrain/`, `_receipts/`). `._`-prefixed files beside every real file
228	are normal AppleDouble xattr sidecars on exFAT, not corruption or duplication.
229	
230	The nightly backup is `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` (pwsh, launchd
231	`com.keystone.dailybackup`), driven by `~/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json`, logging to
232	`~/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log`. `~/.claude` is itself the `dotclaude` repo.
233	Workflow docs live in `~/DEV/Bucket` (`docs/SYSTEM-HEALTH-FINDINGS.md`,
234	`docs/AGENT-FIX-PROMPT.md`, `docs/FIX-STATUS-2026-08-14.md`).

268	## Manifest classification — get this right, it routes athlete data
269	
270	`backup-manifest.json` is default-deny: any `~/DEV` dir absent from `paths[]` fails the
271	health check. Adding an entry requires a human class call:
272	
273	| class | destinations |
274	|---|---|
275	| `institutional` | `ssd`, `baylor` (+`github` if a repo) |
276	| `personal` | `ssd` (+`github` if a repo) |
277	
278	`isRepo: true` also sets `captureOrphans` and `captureWorkingTree` true and needs `remote`.
279	**Athlete data must never be classed `personal`** — `personal` skips the Baylor OneDrive
280	destination. `baylor` is `deprecated: true` and must never be a sole destination.
281	
282	## Traps that cost time
283	
284	- **Milvus is NOT in the memsearch path**, despite what `RESTORE.md` and the Bucket docs
285	  say. Indexing works with port 19530 closed and Docker not installed. Don't set it up.
286	- **`-DryRun` cannot verify a write path.** It passes `rsync -n`, which writes nothing. A
287	  snapshot that fails live will show `OK` in a dry run. Only a non-dry run is evidence.
288	- **Never size up a DriveFS destination with `du`.** It reports local cache/allocated
289	  blocks, not logical size — the `codex/sessions` mirror read as "47 MB of 289 MB" while
290	  actually holding 255 of 256 files, with a 35 MB file verified byte-identical by
291	  `stat -f%z` on both sides. Compare **file counts and per-file byte sizes**, never `du -sh`.
292	- **`snapshot:sessions` is a genuine hang** — not a size problem, not a lock, not a
293	  permission fault, and not slow enumeration. Three wrong theories died here in one
294	  session; see the evidence section below before forming a fourth. **Bounded 2026-08-14**
295	  by a watchdog in `Invoke-Rsync` (900s ceiling, hard SIGKILL, records `rsync-timeout`),
296	  committed as `8863a37`. That caps the symptom so the run reaches the SSD capture. The
297	  wedge itself is still unexplained.
298	- **Tier A memory is NOT in git.** `~/.claude/.gitignore` line 1 is `/*` (default-deny
299	  allowlist) and `projects/` is not allowlisted, so `projects/*/memory/*.md` has exactly
300	  two backup layers: the Drive SNAP of `~/.claude/projects`, and the SSD. With CRASHBOX
301	  unmounted that is a single copy. Nothing to "commit" there — it's by design.
302	- **`daily-backup.ps1` refuses to merge diverged repos by design** — that's correct
303	  behavior, not a bug. Reconcile by hand.
304	- **stack-doctor's cloud heartbeat** watches the newest per-run receipt
305	  (`_receipts/run-*.txt`). It used to watch `RESTORE.md`, which the job *copies*
306	  (`Copy-Item -Force`, line 411) rather than rewrites, so its mtime never advanced and the
307	  check cried `backup-cloud-stale (218h)` while DriveFS was healthy. Fixed 2026-08-14.
308	- **Untracked files block a fast-forward**, and plain `git stash` does not pick them up —
309	  needs `-u`, or rename them aside. Bit the documented SecondBrain fix.
310	- Reading exit codes through a pipe returns the *last* pipeline element's status, not the
311	  command's — see [[zsh-shell-traps]]. This produced two wrong readings in one
312	  session (`rsync ... | tail` and a stack-check run).

356	## `snapshot:sessions` — evidence from a live reproduction, 2026-08-14 15:20 (stack-doctor)
357	
358	Caught the hang in progress and narrowed it. **Root cause still open** — this section is
359	evidence, not a verdict. Everything below is measured, not inferred:
360	
361	- **It is a hang, not a slow transfer.** Four rsync processes (client `-a ... codex/sessions/`,
362	  its `--server` receiver, plus two older receivers) sat at **0.01–0.03 s of CPU across
363	  34–85 minutes** of wall clock. Zero progress, not slow progress.
364	- **Nothing is left to copy.** The mirror is **256/256 files** — the previously-missing
365	  `2026/08/06/rollout-*.jsonl` is present. A complete mirror still hangs.
366	- **The mount is healthy.** A recursive `find` over the destination returned 256 files
367	  promptly, and `touch` inside the exact hung directory succeeded instantly. Reads *and*
368	  writes both work, so this is not a wedged DriveFS/FUSE mount.
369	- **The wedged processes ignore SIGTERM** (still alive minutes later in `S` state) — they
370	  are blocked inside a call that neither returns nor delivers signals.
371	- **Dry runs cannot see it**: `-n` completes clean, live runs hang. Another instance of the
372	  "`-DryRun` cannot verify a write path" trap above.
373	
374	### Orphans are a symptom, not the cause
375	
376	Two `rsync --server` receivers were **orphaned to PPID 1** (started 13:55 and 14:33). It is
377	tempting to call them the blocker; the timeline refutes it — the **10:31:54 run hung at the
378	identical point** (last line `SNAP skip (missing): .codex/memories`, no end line) while the
379	oldest surviving orphan did not exist until 13:55. `kill` on both orphans did not unblock
380	the live pair either.
381	
382	Why they accumulate: **`daily-backup.ps1` contains no `pkill` at all** (verified by grep —
383	do not go looking for one). The anchored `pkill -f "^/usr/bin/rsync"` belongs to an *ad-hoc
384	wrapper used interactively in another session*. That pattern matches only the client, whose
385	`argv[0]` is the full path; the `--server` child's `argv[0]` is bare `rsync`, so
386	`pgrep -f "^/usr/bin/rsync"` returns the client alone. Every kill-and-retry therefore strands
387	one more receiver. If that wrapper is reused, match on `-x rsync` or the destination path.
388	
389	### ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-14 17:00 — it is not rsync
390	
391	Ran the copy in the foreground with `-avv`, unpiped. It printed ~99 lines of
392	`... is uptodate` and froze mid-filename. Then:
393	
394	- `sample <receiver-pid>` showed the process blocked in **`__mmap`** — one frame, not moving.
395	- `lsof` on it showed FD 5 open on a specific **destination** file:
396	  `codex/sessions/2026/05/08/rollout-2026-05-08T17-14-58-019e09a8-*.jsonl`.
397	- **`head -c 512` on that destination file hangs by itself**, with zero rsync processes
398	  running. A plain read. So the file is unreadable through DriveFS.
399	- A 44-file sample elsewhere in the same mirror read instantly, so it is **specific files,
400	  not the mount**.
401	
402	The files are **DriveFS placeholders** — uploaded to Google, then evicted from the local
403	cache. Census of the destination on 2026-08-14: 256 files, **122 materialized (48.5 MB on
404	disk), 134 placeholder-only (240.7 MB logical, 0 bytes local)**. Source is 256/256
405	materialized. Detect with `stat -f '%b %z'`: blocks==0 with a nonzero logical size means
406	the content is not local. Reading one forces an on-demand fetch, and that fetch stalls —
407	which is what blocks `__mmap`. rsync was the victim, not the cause. **Do not chase rsync
408	flags**; the block happens at open, before any comparison strategy applies.
409	
410	**This inverts the problem: the backup is fine, the verification is what's broken.** All
411	256 files are on Google's servers. Nothing is missing. What fails is the *next* run's
412	attempt to re-read them to confirm they match. Never conclude "the snapshot is broken"
413	from this failure mode.
414	
415	Also: `du -sh` on the destination reports the *local cache* (48 MB), not the logical 289 MB.
416	Both numbers are true and mean different things — do not treat the gap as missing data.
417	
418	Diagnostic sequence that worked, reuse it: `sample <pid>` for the blocking syscall →
419	`lsof -p <pid>` for the file it is on → bounded `head -c` on that path to prove the
420	filesystem, not the tool, is at fault.
421	
422	**Attempted fix that DID NOT WORK**: pinning `My Drive/Backups` "Available offline" via the
423	Finder context menu (there is no CLI or xattr for it — the app ships no control surface).
424	Eric pinned it 2026-08-14 17:30. Result: **one** file materialized, then flat for 5 minutes
425	(133 placeholders, 49.2 MB, unchanged). Restarting Drive did not help either.
426	
427	**DriveFS on this Mac is itself unhealthy** — this is the real blocker, not rsync and not
428	the pin:
429	- It refused a graceful `osascript quit` for 20s and needed SIGKILL. Its log emitted
430	  `crashpad ... ThreadsStuck` every 6s. Restarting cleared the stuck threads but nothing else.
431	- The **download** queue fails, not just uploads: `merger.cc:969:ProcessDownloadEvent` +
432	  `HandleFailedChange [DownloadMergeQueueItem]`. DriveFS cannot pull content *down*.
433	- Signs of local DB damage: `item_query_handler.cc:1135:OnGetItemIds Ignoring item
434	  local-376561 that's missing from ...`.
435	- NOT quota: 671 GB used of 5.5 TB.
436	
437	**Do not clear the DriveFS content cache as the remedy.** It converts every materialized
438	file into a placeholder needing re-download, feeding the exact mechanism that is failing —
439	122 readable files could become 0. If DriveFS is repaired, do it by signing out and back in
440	to force a DB rebuild, deliberately, with time to watch it.
441	
442	### RESOLVED 2026-08-14 — the backup was never broken, the verification was
443	
444	**Final mechanism**: files Drive has evicted from local cache are placeholders. Fetching a
445	placeholder through DriveFS is *unreliable* — usually fast, sometimes stalling for tens of
446	minutes. rsync blocking on such a fetch is the entire "wedge". Proof it is a slow fetch and
447	not a poisoned file: the file that hung four separate times **now reads instantly**, and its
448	blocks went 0 → 770,048 — the repeated read attempts eventually completed the fetch. Six
449	other placeholders read fine first try. Nothing was corrupt.
450	
451	**`~/.claude/scripts/verify-drive-backup.sh` (`0d2edb5`) is now the way to verify.** It
452	compares the Drive API's server-side `md5Checksum` against a local md5 — metadata only, no
453	DriveFS read, batched ~25 names per query. First run on `~/.codex/sessions`:
454	**256/256 verified, 0 mismatch, 0 missing.** The snapshot that logged `FAILED` for days was
455	complete and byte-correct the whole time.
456	
457	Do not "fix" this by deleting Drive copies. Both files that hung were verified byte-identical
458	to source *before* anything was touched — deleting would have destroyed a good backup to
459	repair a read path.
460	
461	**It is plain fetch latency, scaling with file size** — no mystery left. A full read-scan of
462	all 256 files with a 6s per-file cap: 33 stalled, and those averaged **2,301 KB vs 1,156 KB
463	for the set overall** (max 15.8 MB). Bigger file, longer fetch. Nothing file-specific,
464	nothing corrupt. The scan itself moved the mirror from 122 → 230 materialized (48.5 → 161.8 MB
465	local), which is exactly what "reading materializes it" predicts.
466	
467	Caution when testing this: **reading a file materializes it**, so any scan warms the cache and
468	a later run passes for reasons that will not hold once Drive evicts again. Timestamp results
469	and never treat a post-scan rsync run as a clean verification.
470	
471	### Why DriveFS is unhealthy — found 2026-08-14 18:20
472	
473	**Google Drive is mirroring `~/DEV` as a device-backup folder named "My Mac"**, including
474	**34 `.git` directories / 3,470 files**. VS Code has `"git.autofetch": true`, which rewrites
475	every repo's `FETCH_HEAD` on a 180s cycle; Drive uploads all 34 each time. That is the source
476	of the `PRECONDITION_FAILED` storms on `FETCH_HEAD` and the stuck threads in `drive_fs.txt`,
477	and therefore of the slow placeholder fetches upstream.
478	
479	Proof (not inference): local `~/DEV/*/.git/FETCH_HEAD` all stamped 18:22:09 while Drive's
480	server copies read `2026-08-14T23:22:09Z` — same second — and the Drive parent chain resolves
481	`FETCH_HEAD → .git → DataBase_GPS_Reporting → DEV → My Mac`.
482	
483	**`OneDrive-Import` was a red herring** — it holds 22 `.git` dirs / 7,292 files, but they are
484	static archives and do not churn. Don't chase it.
485	
486	**FIXED 2026-08-14 ~18:28 — Eric removed `~/DEV` from Drive Preferences → "Folders from your
487	computer" (keeping the cloud copy). Verified, and it worked:**
488	- Server-side `FETCH_HEAD` froze at `23:28:12Z` while local `~/DEV` copies kept updating
489	  (18:32:28) — churn decoupled, `git.autofetch` left ON as intended.
490	- `PRECONDITION_FAILED` 14 → **0**. `ProcessDownloadEvent` errors 11 → **0**.
491	  `HandleFailedChange` stable (idle retry backlog, not growing).
492	- Google Drive CPU **64.6% → 0.0%**.
493	- **End-to-end: 5/5 genuine placeholders (blocks==0) fetched in 2–3s each**, where the same
494	  class of read previously stalled for minutes or indefinitely. This is the actual cure for
495	  the `snapshot:sessions` wedge — the watchdog only bounded it.
496	
497	Original recommendation, for the record: remove `~/DEV` from Drive Preferences → "Folders
498	from your computer", choosing KEEP for the existing cloud copy. The mirror is redundant and
499	strictly worse than the nightly, which already covers `~/DEV` via 68 manifest entries →
500	SSD + GitHub with `.git` excluded and credential files denied (6 projects hit that policy on
501	2026-08-14). **Do not** "fix" this by disabling `git.autofetch`: that masks the symptom, costs
502	a useful feature, and leaves 3,470 `.git` files still mirrored to churn on every commit and
503	checkout. Verify afterward by re-querying `FETCH_HEAD` modifiedTime via the Drive API and
504	re-checking `drive_fs.txt` for `ThreadsStuck` / `PRECONDITION_FAILED`.
505	
506	How to check whether anything is pending before any Drive surgery: sample
507	`grep -c HandleModifiedLocalItem/HandleFailedChange/DownloadMergeQueueItem` in
508	`~/Library/Application Support/Google/DriveFS/Logs/drive_fs.txt` over ~90s — flat counters
509	mean idle queues. **Do not** use the presence of `com.google.drivefs.item-id` as an
510	upload-pending signal: 774 files in Backups lacked it and were all already on the server.
511	
512	Rejected: `--ignore-existing` (would freeze any mid-session rollout file at its partial
513	size in Drive permanently) and leaving the watchdog to absorb it (~15 min wasted nightly,
514	and two standing errors would camouflage real ones).
515	
516	Note `-W` (whole-file) is already default for local transfers, so `--whole-file`,
517	`--size-only` and delta-algorithm tuning are all dead ends here — the block happens on
518	open, before any comparison strategy matters.
519	
520	## The SSD layer's real failure mode — schedule/mount mismatch, found 2026-08-29
521	
522	**The nightly is healthy; the SSD layer is simply absent at run time.** `com.keystone.dailybackup`
523	fires at 00:30 and CRASHBOX is normally unplugged then, so every run logs
524	`TARGET SSD /Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup NOT MOUNTED - orphan and working-tree capture
525	SKIPPED this run` and ends `OK (0 errors)`. A clean exit code is therefore **not** evidence the
526	SSD captured — the skip is not an error. Check `_receipts/run-*.txt` mtime on the drive instead.
527	
528	Receipt history proves the pattern: 10 SSD captures total, clustered on days the drive happened
529	to be attached (Aug 6, Aug 14 ×5, Aug 15, Aug 16, Aug 17), then a **12-day gap** to Aug 29. Eric
530	read this as "the SSD backup has never run"; it had, just rarely.
531	
532	**Manual run is the remedy and takes ~6 minutes**, not the ~45 the 2026-08-14 notes imply:
533	`/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -File ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` (no SSD-only switch exists; do
534	not add one). Run 20260829-073713: Drive SNAPs finished in **6 seconds** — the `codex/sessions`
535	wedge is genuinely gone since the `~/DEV` de-mirroring fix — DEV capture 07:37–07:40, `.claude`/
536	`.codex`/`.gemini`/SecondBrain state 07:41–07:42, `RECEIPT ssd : verified` at 07:42:50,
537	`end: OK (0 errors)` at 07:43:14. SSD 25 → 27 GB. The long tail in the 00:34 nightly was the
538	memsearch INDEX step (00:51→01:18), which runs *after* the backup and is not part of it.
539	
540	Verification trap repeated here: **top-level SSD directory mtimes stay old after a successful
541	capture** (`SecondBrain` still read Aug 17, `claude` Aug 14) because `rsync -a` preserves source
542	mtimes and a parent dir's mtime only moves when an entry is added or removed at that level. The
543	`STATE-SSD ... : OK` log lines and the receipt are the evidence; mtimes are not. See also
544	[[keystoneos-verification-habits]].
545	
546	**RESOLVED 2026-08-29**: schedule moved 00:30 -> 09:00 in
547	`~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.dailybackup.plist` (PlistBuddy `Set :StartCalendarInterval:Hour 9`,
548	then `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.dailybackup` + `bootstrap`; live schedule confirmed
549	`Hour => 9, Minute => 0` via `launchctl print`). Old plist kept at `.plist.bak-2026-08-29`. 09:00 was
550	chosen from mount evidence (drive attached 07:31 on 08-29; the 08-17 capture ran 08:05). **Do not
551	verify this by mtime or by exit code** — the only proof is a fresh `_receipts/run-*.txt` on the drive
552	dated 08-30 or later. If receipts still cluster, the drive is not attached at 09:00 and the hour is wrong.
553	
554	`~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` archived to `.errors.log.archived-2026-08-29` and
555	cleared the same day. It held two **still-open** issues, not stale history: memsearch `onnxruntime`
556	import failure (2026-08-22, corroborated by `INDEX full set: Indexed 0 chunks` on 08-28/08-29), and
557	stack-doctor weekly flagging `errors-log`, `flush-stale`, `memfile-full:MEMORY.md` (2026-08-24).
558	
559	**Both cleared by end of 2026-08-29** — stack-doctor returned `ALL CLEAR`: memsearch `search: OK`,
560	`last-flush.json OK (0h ago)`, no `FLUSH_ERROR` in recent dailies, `errors.log: clean`. The
561	`onnxruntime` import failure did not need a reinstall, so **do not** reflexively run
562	`uv tool install --force memsearch` on the next `ETIMEDOUT` — that strips the local flush patch
563	and creates a worse problem. Confirmed here: `memsearch --version` answered instantly (0.4.17) and
564	`pgrep -fc memsearch` was 0, ruling out both a broken binary and the
565	[[milvus-lock-misdiagnosis]] lock-contention pattern.
566	
567	A separate `memsearch-sync: index ETIMEDOUT Nx consecutively` streak ran 6→13 during the afternoon
568	session of 08-29 and then self-cleared. Per the skill's own note, `Indexed 0 chunks` is usually a
569	starved flush pipeline rather than a dead indexer — **check `flush-stale` before touching
570	memsearch**. The streak counter is reset by the nightly backup, so a climbing count mid-session is
571	expected noise unless it survives a backup run. Both cleared by end of 2026-08-29 —
572	stack-doctor returned ALL CLEAR and the thread is closed.
573	
574	Guard trap: shell truncation (`: > file`) anywhere under `$HOME` is blocked by dcg
575	rule `core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`; `cp /dev/null file` is allowed, and macOS has no
576	`truncate` binary. This file is itself near the `memfile-full` threshold — trim before appending more.
577	
578	## A stalled run with no rsync child = an unanswered macOS access prompt (2026-09-03)
579	
580	`daily-backup.ps1` gates both optional destinations on a bare `Test-Path` with **no timeout**:
581	`Test-Path $GDrive` (section 2a) and `Test-Path $SsdRoot` (section 2b). When macOS has a pending
582	TCC/removable-volume permission prompt for that path, the call blocks **forever** — and because 2a
583	runs before 2b, the SSD capture never happens and no receipt is written.
584	
585	**The tell:** `pwsh` alive in `S`/`SN` state, **zero rsync children**, and the log frozen mid-run.
586	That is not a slow copy — a slow copy always shows an `rsync` process. `ps -axo pid,stat,comm` on
587	macOS marks I/O wait `U`, not `D`; a `D`-state grep finds nothing and proves nothing.
588	
589	**The fix is the human, not the shell — look at the screen for a pending prompt FIRST.** On
590	2026-09-03 both `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-*` and `/Volumes/CRASHBOX` were unresponsive to
591	a plain `ls`. The Drive half cleared after a quit/relaunch of Google Drive, **but Eric was
592	approving access prompts in that same window — the relaunch is unproven and may have done nothing.**
593	Do not treat killing Google Drive as the known fix. The SSD half cleared only when he approved the
594	prompt. **Do not force-unmount CRASHBOX** (exFAT, no journal) — ask first.
595	
596	Probably (unverified): the Claude Code shell and the launchd/reconcile jobs are different TCC
597	principals, so this prompt should not recur for the scheduled runs — but it may fire once per new
598	app that launches the script.
599	
600	**Never re-run without `pkill -f daily-backup.ps1` first.** A hung run is harmless, but several hung
601	runs unblock *together* the moment access is granted and race onto the SSD — the two-writer
602	corruption this whole system exists to prevent.
603	
604	**Timing that matters:** reconcile replays the backup at 07:00 if no `OK` is logged for today, and
605	launchd fires at 09:00 regardless (see "Current state" above). A manual run finishing before 07:00
606	suppresses the replay; one finishing after 07:00 can collide with it.
607	
608	Open gap, not yet fixed: neither `Test-Path` has a watchdog, unlike `Invoke-Rsync`
609	(`$RsyncTimeoutSec = 900`). Worth wrapping both.
610	
611	## `/backup` skill + the completeness signal (2026-09-04)
612	
613	`~/.claude/skills/backup/SKILL.md` is the on-demand path — the launchd job only fires if the
614	Mac is awake at 09:00. Standing routine: plug in CRASHBOX, then type `/backup`.
615	
616	**Job count, not error count, is the completeness signal.** A run with CRASHBOX unmounted
617	reports `OK (0 errors)` with **9 jobs**; the same run with it attached reports **31 jobs**.
618	Never report "backup complete" from a 0-error run without checking `okCount` and naming any
619	skipped target.
620	
621	`repo-push:*` failures are usually a transient `Could not resolve host: github.com`, not a
622	credential or repo problem — commits are already local, so a re-run pushes them. Seen
623	2026-09-04 09:05 on `global-memory` and `skills`; one re-run cleared both.
624	
625	A USB-C drive that powers on but never mounts is almost always a charge-only cable.
626	`diskutil list external` printing nothing at all is the fast check — that is a cable/port
627	problem, not software.
628	
629	Full handoff: `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/2026-09-04-backup-skill.md`.
630	
631	## Manifest coverage closed + job-count baseline reset (2026-09-09)
632	
633	**The 49 `manifest-unmanaged` folders are gone.** They were never a classification backlog —
634	they were fallout from the GitHub consolidation migration (see [[github-consolidation]]).
635	All 49 added to `backup-manifest.json` in one pass: 47 are git repos with `erash11` remotes
636	(`isRepo:true`, `captureOrphans`/`captureWorkingTree` true, destinations `["ssd","github"]`),
637	and 2 are plain dirs — `_ARCHIVE` (4.3 GB) and `docs` — destinations `["ssd"]` only.
638	`baylor` deliberately omitted from every new entry; it is deprecated and Eric's own newest
639	entry (`DEV/Life-OS`, commit `3444c0b`) already omits it.
640	
641	**`class` is inert.** Grep of `daily-backup.ps1` shows it is read nowhere — only `isRepo`,
642	`captureOrphans`, `captureWorkingTree` and `destinations` drive behavior. The
643	institutional/personal call is documentation. Do not stall a manifest add waiting on it.
644	
645	**A DEV manifest entry never auto-commits or pushes that repo.** `Sync-Repo` is called on a
646	hardcoded list (SecondBrain, global-memory, skills, dotclaude); the manifest loop only calls
647	`Capture-RepoData` (SSD) or `Snapshot-Additive`. Adding 47 project repos was therefore safe
648	with open PRs and dirty trees — verify from source before assuming otherwise.
649	
650	**Job-count baseline is now 76, not 31.** The 2026-09-04 note above (9 = no SSD, 31 = SSD
651	attached) is superseded. Full run with CRASHBOX attached = **76 jobs**. `CAPTURE` only logs a
652	line when a repo has files git does not carry, so 18 log lines with 65 capture jobs is normal —
653	read `okCount`, not the log line count.
654	
655	**Removed 2 dead entries**: `DEV/AI_Analyst` and `DEV/token-dashboard`. Both had moved into
656	`~/DEV/_ARCHIVE/`, which is itself now backed up, so coverage was preserved, not dropped.
657	`DexaProject` stays declared-but-absent on purpose — it lives on Google Drive.
658	
659	**`~/.claude` now tracks session transcripts.** Eric's commit `8a3d55c` (2026-09-09 15:44)
660	un-ignored `projects/`, so the dotclaude repo carries ~368 MB of `.jsonl` transcripts and
661	Tier A memory. This **invalidates the "Tier A memory is NOT in git" trap above** — it now has
662	a third layer. No single file exceeds 40 MB, so pushes succeed; they are just slower.
663	
664	Full handoff: `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/2026-09-09-backup-manifest-coverage.md`.

=== project_automation-cadence.md

name: automation-cadence

metadata:

Durable schedule and capability facts for the Mac automation stack. These are stable
settings, not active threads — health-check them with `/claude-stack-doctor`.

## Ritual nudges (launchd `com.keystone.rituals`)

- **Weekdays 17:00** → `/interview-me`
- **Fridays 15:30** → `/weekly-review`
- `harvest` and `forecast-capture` also run through `ritual-check.ps1`; their
  due/overdue state is computed from their own output, not from a fixed clock
  (forecast-capture is Monday-anchored and season-bounded — see
  [[cfb-forecast-capture]]). Four rituals total; `Name    = ` in
  `KeystoneOS/scripts/ritual-check.ps1` is the authoritative list.

The nudge is only a prompt; **the output artifact is the record**, not the reminder firing.

## memsearch reindex

Reindex **rides the daily backup task** rather than running on its own timer. The
nightly moved 00:30 → **09:00 on 2026-08-29** (CRASHBOX was unplugged at 00:30), so
any reasoning that assumes an overnight reindex is wrong — the backup's uncapped full reindex absorbs backlogs the
short SessionEnd hook can't finish. See [[backup-sync-system]].

## OS audits

Full OS audit last run **2026-07-24** (reports under `audits/`, guards auto-run);
**next due 2026-10-24**.

## Capability limits worth remembering

- **gws** is authenticated. Re-auth requires explicit full scope URLs — the `-s drive`
  shorthand silently grants no scopes (v0.22.5 bug), and `~/.config/gws/token_cache.json`
  must be deleted after re-auth or the stale token is served. See [[gws-forms-api]].
- **MCP Gmail is draft-only** — it can compose drafts but must not be treated as a send path.

## reMarkable OCR

`remarkable_extract.py` — USB-first with a `--cloud` fallback; Vision API key lives in
`.env`.
=== project_command-centre.md
---
name: command-centre
description: "The DEV front door — always-on read-only status page at http://localhost:7373, plus the rules that keep it trustworthy"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b7d080c1-e0f8-4eb5-b181-d06b87224449
  modified: 2026-09-02T01:44:00.951Z
---

**Built 2026-08-31.** Closes ARMS gap 5. `~/DEV/CommandCentre/server.py`, served by
`com.keystone.commandcentre` (`RunAtLoad` + `KeepAlive`), own `DESIGN.md`.

**<http://localhost:7373>** — one page answering "is anything broken?": agent
health, backup result, graph progress, logged failures, active projects, and
links to every generated report with its age.

Design rules that must hold, each learned the hard way:

- **Standard library only.** Python 3.14 here is PEP 668-managed, so any
  dependency means a venv to maintain forever. A read-only local page never
  earns that.
- **Rendered fresh per request.** Never cached, never regenerated on a timer. A
  page that can be stale is a page you stop believing — that is exactly why the
  on-demand `project-triage/dashboard.html` never became a front door.
- **A dashboard that contradicts the CLI is worse than no dashboard.** The file
  counter first used `total - len(done)` and disagreed with `gf_remaining.py` by
  13, because the done-list holds entries no longer in the corpus. It now does
  the same **set difference**, and the corpus selection is kept identical across
  `server.py`, `gf_gemini.py` and `gf_remaining.py`.
- **Judge a running service on its PID, not its last exit code.** A `KeepAlive`
  daemon carries the exit code of the instance that *died*, so a restart leaves a
  nonzero code behind permanently. `launchctl list`'s first column is the PID and
  the second is that stale status — reading the wrong column makes a healthy
  service look broken.
- **Live `launchctl` state is the truth**; `run-ledger.json` is shown but never
  allowed to claim a job succeeded. See [[keystoneos-verification-habits]].
- **Every source is optional** — a missing input renders "unknown", never a 500.
- **Bound to `127.0.0.1` only**, which is why it needs no auth. Do not change the
  bind address without adding one. Read-only on purpose: no buttons, so a stray
  browser tab cannot fire an agent. `~/.claude/scripts/skill-button.sh` exists
  for the day buttons are wanted.

**The threat to a localhost service is a web page you visit, not the network.**
Any site your browser opens can make requests to `127.0.0.1`, so binding to
loopback is not a security boundary on its own. **DNS rebinding** is the real
attack: the attacker's domain re-resolves to `127.0.0.1`, their JavaScript
becomes same-origin, and it reads everything. The defence is a **`Host` header
allowlist** — refuse any request whose Host is not a loopback name. Three review
rounds were needed to get the parsing right: compare IPv6 numerically (so
`[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]` is recognised), refuse a second `Host` header rather than
guess, strip exactly one trailing DNS dot, and validate the port range. Also
learned: **curl silently collapses duplicate headers** — prove that guard over a
raw socket.

**An allowlisted name is not an allowlisted file.** `Path.exists()` and
`read_bytes()` follow symlinks, so an exact-path allowlist still served
`/etc/hosts` when the target was swapped for a symlink. Confine the resolved
object too, then **read through the same descriptor you checked** (`O_NOFOLLOW`,
then compare the fd's `(st_dev, st_ino)` to the pre-check `lstat`) — checking a
path and reopening it by name is a check/use race. Close the fd in a `finally`
that catches every exception type, not just `OSError`.

**Any number shown in two places must be computed by identical code.** A page
that contradicts the CLI destroys trust in both. Three separate counters here
had to be aligned four times: set difference not arithmetic, the same corpus
selection, the same skip gates, the same `GF_MAXBYTES` env override — including
its "0 means no cap" convention — and the gate applied to a progress line's
numerator *and* denominator.

**Creating any new `~/DEV/<folder>` breaks the backup immediately** — the manifest
is default-deny, so `daily-backup` exits 1 until the folder is added to
`~/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json`. Working as designed; just add the entry
in the same turn. The `class` field answers *who keeps this when you leave

`keystone-reconcile.ps1` is a **generic make-up engine**. It has no mention of `daily-backup` at
all; it loops the registry at `DEV/KeystoneOS/data/jobs.json` and calls
`run-job.ps1 -Job <id> -Trigger reconcile -MadeUp` for any job with no success recorded today.

- **If no successful run is recorded by 07:00, reconcile replays it** → the ~07:00-07:10 run.
- **launchd `com.keystone.dailybackup` fires at 09:00 regardless** → the second run.
- **Run the backup by hand before 07:00 and reconcile skips it** ("already succeeded today").
  Confirmed 09-03: a 06:15 manual run logged `OK` at 06:25, and no 07:00 run happened.

plist fires at 09:00. The make-up window is what actually drives the 07:00 replay, so the stale

`backup-manifest.json` is default-deny: any `~/DEV` dir absent from `paths[]` fails the

  snapshot that fails live will show `OK` in a dry run. Only a non-dry run is evidence.
- **Never size up a DriveFS destination with `du`.** It reports local cache/allocated
  blocks, not logical size — the `codex/sessions` mirror read as "47 MB of 289 MB" while
  actually holding 255 of 256 files, with a 35 MB file verified byte-identical by
  `stat -f%z` on both sides. Compare **file counts and per-file byte sizes**, never `du -sh`.
- **`snapshot:sessions` is a genuine hang** — not a size problem, not a lock, not a
  permission fault, and not slow enumeration. Three wrong theories died here in one
  session; see the evidence section below before forming a fourth. **Bounded 2026-08-14**

  wedge itself is still unexplained.
- **Tier A memory is NOT in git.** `~/.claude/.gitignore` line 1 is `/*` (default-deny
  allowlist) and `projects/` is not allowlisted, so `projects/*/memory/*.md` has exactly
  two backup layers: the Drive SNAP of `~/.claude/projects`, and the SSD. With CRASHBOX
  unmounted that is a single copy. Nothing to "commit" there — it's by design.
- **`daily-backup.ps1` refuses to merge diverged repos by design** — that's correct
  behavior, not a bug. Reconcile by hand.
- **stack-doctor's cloud heartbeat** watches the newest per-run receipt
  (`_receipts/run-*.txt`). It used to watch `RESTORE.md`, which the job *copies*

- Reading exit codes through a pipe returns the *last* pipeline element's status, not the

## `snapshot:sessions` — evidence from a live reproduction, 2026-08-14 15:20 (stack-doctor)

Caught the hang in progress and narrowed it. **Root cause still open** — this section is
evidence, not a verdict. Everything below is measured, not inferred:

- **It is a hang, not a slow transfer.** Four rsync processes (client `-a ... codex/sessions/`,
  its `--server` receiver, plus two older receivers) sat at **0.01–0.03 s of CPU across
  34–85 minutes** of wall clock. Zero progress, not slow progress.
- **Nothing is left to copy.** The mirror is **256/256 files** — the previously-missing
  `2026/08/06/rollout-*.jsonl` is present. A complete mirror still hangs.
- **The mount is healthy.** A recursive `find` over the destination returned 256 files
  promptly, and `touch` inside the exact hung directory succeeded instantly. Reads *and*
  writes both work, so this is not a wedged DriveFS/FUSE mount.
- **The wedged processes ignore SIGTERM** (still alive minutes later in `S` state) — they
  are blocked inside a call that neither returns nor delivers signals.
- **Dry runs cannot see it**: `-n` completes clean, live runs hang. Another instance of the
  "`-DryRun` cannot verify a write path" trap above.

### Orphans are a symptom, not the cause

Two `rsync --server` receivers were **orphaned to PPID 1** (started 13:55 and 14:33). It is
tempting to call them the blocker; the timeline refutes it — the **10:31:54 run hung at the
identical point** (last line `SNAP skip (missing): .codex/memories`, no end line) while the
oldest surviving orphan did not exist until 13:55. `kill` on both orphans did not unblock
the live pair either.

Why they accumulate: **`daily-backup.ps1` contains no `pkill` at all** (verified by grep —
do not go looking for one). The anchored `pkill -f "^/usr/bin/rsync"` belongs to an *ad-hoc
wrapper used interactively in another session*. That pattern matches only the client, whose
`argv[0]` is the full path; the `--server` child's `argv[0]` is bare `rsync`, so
`pgrep -f "^/usr/bin/rsync"` returns the client alone. Every kill-and-retry therefore strands
one more receiver. If that wrapper is reused, match on `-x rsync` or the destination path.

### ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-14 17:00 — it is not rsync

Ran the copy in the foreground with `-avv`, unpiped. It printed ~99 lines of
`... is uptodate` and froze mid-filename. Then:

- `sample <receiver-pid>` showed the process blocked in **`__mmap`** — one frame, not moving.
- `lsof` on it showed FD 5 open on a specific **destination** file:
  `codex/sessions/2026/05/08/rollout-2026-05-08T17-14-58-019e09a8-*.jsonl`.
- **`head -c 512` on that destination file hangs by itself**, with zero rsync processes
  running. A plain read. So the file is unreadable through DriveFS.
- A 44-file sample elsewhere in the same mirror read instantly, so it is **specific files,
  not the mount**.

The files are **DriveFS placeholders** — uploaded to Google, then evicted from the local
cache. Census of the destination on 2026-08-14: 256 files, **122 materialized (48.5 MB on
disk), 134 placeholder-only (240.7 MB logical, 0 bytes local)**. Source is 256/256
materialized. Detect with `stat -f '%b %z'`: blocks==0 with a nonzero logical size means
the content is not local. Reading one forces an on-demand fetch, and that fetch stalls —
which is what blocks `__mmap`. rsync was the victim, not the cause. **Do not chase rsync
flags**; the block happens at open, before any comparison strategy applies.

**This inverts the problem: the backup is fine, the verification is what's broken.** All
256 files are on Google's servers. Nothing is missing. What fails is the *next* run's
attempt to re-read them to confirm they match. Never conclude "the snapshot is broken"
from this failure mode.

Also: `du -sh` on the destination reports the *local cache* (48 MB), not the logical 289 MB.
Both numbers are true and mean different things — do not treat the gap as missing data.

Diagnostic sequence that worked, reuse it: `sample <pid>` for the blocking syscall →
`lsof -p <pid>` for the file it is on → bounded `head -c` on that path to prove the
filesystem, not the tool, is at fault.

**Attempted fix that DID NOT WORK**: pinning `My Drive/Backups` "Available offline" via the
Finder context menu (there is no CLI or xattr for it — the app ships no control surface).
Eric pinned it 2026-08-14 17:30. Result: **one** file materialized, then flat for 5 minutes
(133 placeholders, 49.2 MB, unchanged). Restarting Drive did not help either.

**DriveFS on this Mac is itself unhealthy** — this is the real blocker, not rsync and not
the pin:
- It refused a graceful `osascript quit` for 20s and needed SIGKILL. Its log emitted
  `crashpad ... ThreadsStuck` every 6s. Restarting cleared the stuck threads but nothing else.
- The **download** queue fails, not just uploads: `merger.cc:969:ProcessDownloadEvent` +
  `HandleFailedChange [DownloadMergeQueueItem]`. DriveFS cannot pull content *down*.
- Signs of local DB damage: `item_query_handler.cc:1135:OnGetItemIds Ignoring item
  local-376561 that's missing from ...`.
- NOT quota: 671 GB used of 5.5 TB.

**Do not clear the DriveFS content cache as the remedy.** It converts every materialized
file into a placeholder needing re-download, feeding the exact mechanism that is failing —
122 readable files could become 0. If DriveFS is repaired, do it by signing out and back in
to force a DB rebuild, deliberately, with time to watch it.

### RESOLVED 2026-08-14 — the backup was never broken, the verification was

**Final mechanism**: files Drive has evicted from local cache are placeholders. Fetching a
placeholder through DriveFS is *unreliable* — usually fast, sometimes stalling for tens of
minutes. rsync blocking on such a fetch is the entire "wedge". Proof it is a slow fetch and
not a poisoned file: the file that hung four separate times **now reads instantly**, and its
blocks went 0 → 770,048 — the repeated read attempts eventually completed the fetch. Six
other placeholders read fine first try. Nothing was corrupt.

**`~/.claude/scripts/verify-drive-backup.sh` (`0d2edb5`) is now the way to verify.** It
compares the Drive API's server-side `md5Checksum` against a local md5 — metadata only, no
DriveFS read, batched ~25 names per query. First run on `~/.codex/sessions`:
**256/256 verified, 0 mismatch, 0 missing.** The snapshot that logged `FAILED` for days was
complete and byte-correct the whole time.

Do not "fix" this by deleting Drive copies. Both files that hung were verified byte-identical
to source *before* anything was touched — deleting would have destroyed a good backup to
repair a read path.

**It is plain fetch latency, scaling with file size** — no mystery left. A full read-scan of
all 256 files with a 6s per-file cap: 33 stalled, and those averaged **2,301 KB vs 1,156 KB
for the set overall** (max 15.8 MB). Bigger file, longer fetch. Nothing file-specific,
nothing corrupt. The scan itself moved the mirror from 122 → 230 materialized (48.5 → 161.8 MB
local), which is exactly what "reading materializes it" predicts.

Caution when testing this: **reading a file materializes it**, so any scan warms the cache and
a later run passes for reasons that will not hold once Drive evicts again. Timestamp results
and never treat a post-scan rsync run as a clean verification.

### Why DriveFS is unhealthy — found 2026-08-14 18:20

**Google Drive is mirroring `~/DEV` as a device-backup folder named "My Mac"**, including
**34 `.git` directories / 3,470 files**. VS Code has `"git.autofetch": true`, which rewrites
every repo's `FETCH_HEAD` on a 180s cycle; Drive uploads all 34 each time. That is the source
of the `PRECONDITION_FAILED` storms on `FETCH_HEAD` and the stuck threads in `drive_fs.txt`,
and therefore of the slow placeholder fetches upstream.

Proof (not inference): local `~/DEV/*/.git/FETCH_HEAD` all stamped 18:22:09 while Drive's
server copies read `2026-08-14T23:22:09Z` — same second — and the Drive parent chain resolves
`FETCH_HEAD → .git → DataBase_GPS_Reporting → DEV → My Mac`.

**`OneDrive-Import` was a red herring** — it holds 22 `.git` dirs / 7,292 files, but they are
static archives and do not churn. Don't chase it.

**FIXED 2026-08-14 ~18:28 — Eric removed `~/DEV` from Drive Preferences → "Folders from your
computer" (keeping the cloud copy). Verified, and it worked:**
- Server-side `FETCH_HEAD` froze at `23:28:12Z` while local `~/DEV` copies kept updating
  (18:32:28) — churn decoupled, `git.autofetch` left ON as intended.
- `PRECONDITION_FAILED` 14 → **0**. `ProcessDownloadEvent` errors 11 → **0**.
  `HandleFailedChange` stable (idle retry backlog, not growing).
- Google Drive CPU **64.6% → 0.0%**.
- **End-to-end: 5/5 genuine placeholders (blocks==0) fetched in 2–3s each**, where the same
  class of read previously stalled for minutes or indefinitely. This is the actual cure for
  the `snapshot:sessions` wedge — the watchdog only bounded it.

Original recommendation, for the record: remove `~/DEV` from Drive Preferences → "Folders
from your computer", choosing KEEP for the existing cloud copy. The mirror is redundant and
strictly worse than the nightly, which already covers `~/DEV` via 68 manifest entries →
SSD + GitHub with `.git` excluded and credential files denied (6 projects hit that policy on
2026-08-14). **Do not** "fix" this by disabling `git.autofetch`: that masks the symptom, costs
a useful feature, and leaves 3,470 `.git` files still mirrored to churn on every commit and
checkout. Verify afterward by re-querying `FETCH_HEAD` modifiedTime via the Drive API and
re-checking `drive_fs.txt` for `ThreadsStuck` / `PRECONDITION_FAILED`.

How to check whether anything is pending before any Drive surgery: sample
`grep -c HandleModifiedLocalItem/HandleFailedChange/DownloadMergeQueueItem` in
`~/Library/Application Support/Google/DriveFS/Logs/drive_fs.txt` over ~90s — flat counters
mean idle queues. **Do not** use the presence of `com.google.drivefs.item-id` as an
upload-pending signal: 774 files in Backups lacked it and were all already on the server.

Rejected: `--ignore-existing` (would freeze any mid-session rollout file at its partial
size in Drive permanently) and leaving the watchdog to absorb it (~15 min wasted nightly,
and two standing errors would camouflage real ones).

Note `-W` (whole-file) is already default for local transfers, so `--whole-file`,
`--size-only` and delta-algorithm tuning are all dead ends here — the block happens on
open, before any comparison strategy matters.

## The SSD layer's real failure mode — schedule/mount mismatch, found 2026-08-29

**The nightly is healthy; the SSD layer is simply absent at run time.** `com.keystone.dailybackup`
fires at 00:30 and CRASHBOX is normally unplugged then, so every run logs
`TARGET SSD /Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup NOT MOUNTED - orphan and working-tree capture
SKIPPED this run` and ends `OK (0 errors)`. A clean exit code is therefore **not** evidence the
SSD captured — the skip is not an error. Check `_receipts/run-*.txt` mtime on the drive instead.

Receipt history proves the pattern: 10 SSD captures total, clustered on days the drive happened
to be attached (Aug 6, Aug 14 ×5, Aug 15, Aug 16, Aug 17), then a **12-day gap** to Aug 29. Eric

not add one). Run 20260829-073713: Drive SNAPs finished in **6 seconds** — the `codex/sessions`
wedge is genuinely gone since the `~/DEV` de-mirroring fix — DEV capture 07:37–07:40, `.claude`/
`.codex`/`.gemini`/SecondBrain state 07:41–07:42, `RECEIPT ssd : verified` at 07:42:50,
`end: OK (0 errors)` at 07:43:14. SSD 25 → 27 GB. The long tail in the 00:34 nightly was the
memsearch INDEX step (00:51→01:18), which runs *after* the backup and is not part of it.

Verification trap repeated here: **top-level SSD directory mtimes stay old after a successful
capture** (`SecondBrain` still read Aug 17, `claude` Aug 14) because `rsync -a` preserves source
mtimes and a parent dir's mtime only moves when an entry is added or removed at that level. The
`STATE-SSD ... : OK` log lines and the receipt are the evidence; mtimes are not. See also
[[keystoneos-verification-habits]].

**RESOLVED 2026-08-29**: schedule moved 00:30 -> 09:00 in
`~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.dailybackup.plist` (PlistBuddy `Set :StartCalendarInterval:Hour 9`,
then `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.dailybackup` + `bootstrap`; live schedule confirmed
`Hour => 9, Minute => 0` via `launchctl print`). Old plist kept at `.plist.bak-2026-08-29`. 09:00 was
chosen from mount evidence (drive attached 07:31 on 08-29; the 08-17 capture ran 08:05). **Do not
verify this by mtime or by exit code** — the only proof is a fresh `_receipts/run-*.txt` on the drive
dated 08-30 or later. If receipts still cluster, the drive is not attached at 09:00 and the hour is wrong.

`~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` archived to `.errors.log.archived-2026-08-29` and
cleared the same day. It held two **still-open** issues, not stale history: memsearch `onnxruntime`
import failure (2026-08-22, corroborated by `INDEX full set: Indexed 0 chunks` on 08-28/08-29), and
stack-doctor weekly flagging `errors-log`, `flush-stale`, `memfile-full:MEMORY.md` (2026-08-24).

**Both cleared by end of 2026-08-29** — stack-doctor returned `ALL CLEAR`: memsearch `search: OK`,
`last-flush.json OK (0h ago)`, no `FLUSH_ERROR` in recent dailies, `errors.log: clean`. The
`onnxruntime` import failure did not need a reinstall, so **do not** reflexively run
`uv tool install --force memsearch` on the next `ETIMEDOUT` — that strips the local flush patch
and creates a worse problem. Confirmed here: `memsearch --version` answered instantly (0.4.17) and
`pgrep -fc memsearch` was 0, ruling out both a broken binary and the
[[milvus-lock-misdiagnosis]] lock-contention pattern.

A separate `memsearch-sync: index ETIMEDOUT Nx consecutively` streak ran 6→13 during the afternoon
session of 08-29 and then self-cleared. Per the skill's own note, `Indexed 0 chunks` is usually a
starved flush pipeline rather than a dead indexer — **check `flush-stale` before touching
memsearch**. The streak counter is reset by the nightly backup, so a climbing count mid-session is
expected noise unless it survives a backup run. Both cleared by end of 2026-08-29 —
stack-doctor returned ALL CLEAR and the thread is closed.

Guard trap: shell truncation (`: > file`) anywhere under `$HOME` is blocked by dcg
rule `core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`; `cp /dev/null file` is allowed, and macOS has no
`truncate` binary. This file is itself near the `memfile-full` threshold — trim before appending more.

## A stalled run with no rsync child = an unanswered macOS access prompt (2026-09-03)

`daily-backup.ps1` gates both optional destinations on a bare `Test-Path` with **no timeout**:
`Test-Path $GDrive` (section 2a) and `Test-Path $SsdRoot` (section 2b). When macOS has a pending
TCC/removable-volume permission prompt for that path, the call blocks **forever** — and because 2a
runs before 2b, the SSD capture never happens and no receipt is written.

**The tell:** `pwsh` alive in `S`/`SN` state, **zero rsync children**, and the log frozen mid-run.
That is not a slow copy — a slow copy always shows an `rsync` process. `ps -axo pid,stat,comm` on
macOS marks I/O wait `U`, not `D`; a `D`-state grep finds nothing and proves nothing.

**The fix is the human, not the shell — look at the screen for a pending prompt FIRST.** On
2026-09-03 both `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-*` and `/Volumes/CRASHBOX` were unresponsive to
a plain `ls`. The Drive half cleared after a quit/relaunch of Google Drive, **but Eric was
approving access prompts in that same window — the relaunch is unproven and may have done nothing.**
Do not treat killing Google Drive as the known fix. The SSD half cleared only when he approved the
prompt. **Do not force-unmount CRASHBOX** (exFAT, no journal) — ask first.

Probably (unverified): the Claude Code shell and the launchd/reconcile jobs are different TCC
principals, so this prompt should not recur for the scheduled runs — but it may fire once per new
app that launches the script.

**Never re-run without `pkill -f daily-backup.ps1` first.** A hung run is harmless, but several hung
runs unblock *together* the moment access is granted and race onto the SSD — the two-writer
corruption this whole system exists to prevent.

**Timing that matters:** reconcile replays the backup at 07:00 if no `OK` is logged for today, and
launchd fires at 09:00 regardless (see "Current state" above). A manual run finishing before 07:00
suppresses the replay; one finishing after 07:00 can collide with it.

Open gap, not yet fixed: neither `Test-Path` has a watchdog, unlike `Invoke-Rsync`
(`$RsyncTimeoutSec = 900`). Worth wrapping both.

## `/backup` skill + the completeness signal (2026-09-04)

`~/.claude/skills/backup/SKILL.md` is the on-demand path — the launchd job only fires if the
Mac is awake at 09:00. Standing routine: plug in CRASHBOX, then type `/backup`.

**Job count, not error count, is the completeness signal.** A run with CRASHBOX unmounted
reports `OK (0 errors)` with **9 jobs**; the same run with it attached reports **31 jobs**.
Never report "backup complete" from a 0-error run without checking `okCount` and naming any
skipped target.

`repo-push:*` failures are usually a transient `Could not resolve host: github.com`, not a
credential or repo problem — commits are already local, so a re-run pushes them. Seen
2026-09-04 09:05 on `global-memory` and `skills`; one re-run cleared both.

A USB-C drive that powers on but never mounts is almost always a charge-only cable.
`diskutil list external` printing nothing at all is the fast check — that is a cable/port
problem, not software.

Full handoff: `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/2026-09-04-backup-skill.md`.

**The 49 `manifest-unmanaged` folders are gone.** They were never a classification backlog —
they were fallout from the GitHub consolidation migration (see [[github-consolidation]]).
All 49 added to `backup-manifest.json` in one pass: 47 are git repos with `erash11` remotes
(`isRepo:true`, `captureOrphans`/`captureWorkingTree` true, destinations `["ssd","github"]`),
and 2 are plain dirs — `_ARCHIVE` (4.3 GB) and `docs` — destinations `["ssd"]` only.
`baylor` deliberately omitted from every new entry; it is deprecated and Eric's own newest
entry (`DEV/Life-OS`, commit `3444c0b`) already omits it.

**`class` is inert.** Grep of `daily-backup.ps1` shows it is read nowhere — only `isRepo`,
`captureOrphans`, `captureWorkingTree` and `destinations` drive behavior. The
institutional/personal call is documentation. Do not stall a manifest add waiting on it.

**A DEV manifest entry never auto-commits or pushes that repo.** `Sync-Repo` is called on a
hardcoded list (SecondBrain, global-memory, skills, dotclaude); the manifest loop only calls
`Capture-RepoData` (SSD) or `Snapshot-Additive`. Adding 47 project repos was therefore safe
with open PRs and dirty trees — verify from source before assuming otherwise.

**Job-count baseline is now 76, not 31.** The 2026-09-04 note above (9 = no SSD, 31 = SSD
attached) is superseded. Full run with CRASHBOX attached = **76 jobs**. `CAPTURE` only logs a
line when a repo has files git does not carry, so 18 log lines with 65 capture jobs is normal —
read `okCount`, not the log line count.

**Removed 2 dead entries**: `DEV/AI_Analyst` and `DEV/token-dashboard`. Both had moved into
`~/DEV/_ARCHIVE/`, which is itself now backed up, so coverage was preserved, not dropped.
`DexaProject` stays declared-but-absent on purpose — it lives on Google Drive.

**`~/.claude` now tracks session transcripts.** Eric's commit `8a3d55c` (2026-09-09 15:44)
un-ignored `projects/`, so the dotclaude repo carries ~368 MB of `.jsonl` transcripts and
Tier A memory. This **invalidates the "Tier A memory is NOT in git" trap above** — it now has
a third layer. No single file exceeds 40 MB, so pushes succeed; they are just slower.

Full handoff: `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/2026-09-09-backup-manifest-coverage.md`.

---
name: cfb-forecast-capture
description: "CFB Victory Model weekly forecast freeze — all 16 Big 12 teams via scripts/weekly_run.sh, archive mirror, Monday-anchored nag 2026-08-24 to 2027-01-23, no backfill, and how to tell a real missed week from a stale snapshot"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 330c1f71-242a-47c7-ac7b-129bd6f5dd3c
  modified: 2026-09-02T19:20:41.051Z
---

The CFB Victory Model's pre-game forecasts are frozen once per week by the
`/forecast-capture` skill, which snapshots predictions **before kickoff** and reports what
moved since the prior week.

## Scope and entry point (changed 2026-09-02, per Eric)

- **All 16 Big 12 teams every week**, not Baylor only. The list is the `BIG12` constant in
  `weekly_capture.py` — one home; do not copy team lists into the wrapper or the skill.
  `--teams`/`--team` still narrow a run. Budget ~10 min for the full sweep.
- **One entry point:** `~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh` (capture → compare
  `--all --archive`). It hardcodes the absolute `uv` path.
- **Archive mirror:** every snapshot and comparison is copied to
  `~/DEV/CFB_Forecast_Archive/<season>/`. Read-only copy; truth stays in
  `CFB_Victory_Model/data/`. Registered in `backup-manifest.json` as `personal`/ssd —
  see [[backup-sync-system]] for why a new `~/DEV` folder must be added there.
- The ritual guard still keys off the newest `*_baylor.csv`, which the Big 12 sweep always
  writes, so detection is unaffected.

## A gap can mean the other machine captured it

Confirmed 2026-09-09. The Mac's `data/weekly_forecast_log.csv` looked like it had
missed 2026-08-26 and 2026-08-31 — it jumped 07-31 → 09-02. Neither week was
missed. **Both were captured on the Windows box**, which runs the same wrapper
against the same repo. The two machines had diverged, each holding captures the
other lacked.

Before declaring a missed week, check the other machine's copy of the log.
Merging is safe: the natural key is `(captured_at, season, team, week, game_id)`,
and a union on that key had **zero conflicts** across 216 Mac + 348 Windows rows
→ 540. Same key never carried different values. See [[github-consolidation]].

## An old newest-snapshot file is not proof of a missed week

Checked 2026-09-02: the newest snapshot was `2026-07-31_baylor.csv`, and both the skill and
COMMANDS.md asserted the 08-24 and 08-31 weeks were "gone for good". They were not — Baylor's
opener was 2026-09-05, so no game had been played and nothing had been overwritten. **A week
is lost only if a game was actually played inside the gap.** Verify before declaring a loss:

```
curl -s "https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/football/college-football/teams/239/schedule?season=2026"
```

(239 = Baylor; read each event's `status.type.name`.) Both docs were corrected.

## Cadence

- ~~**Wednesdays**, season window **2026-08-26 → 2027-01-20**~~ — superseded
  2026-08-15. Current cadence is **Monday-anchored**, season window
  **2026-08-24 → 2027-01-23**. See "Cadence" below, which is authoritative.

## The constraint that makes the cadence non-negotiable

**There is no backfill.** A pre-game forecast is only capturable before the game is played;
a missed week is permanently missing from the series, not a chore that rolls
forward. This is why the reminder escalates rather than silently re-queuing.

## Mac-side guard (built 2026-08-15)

`ritual-check.ps1` now carries a fourth ritual, `forecast-capture`, so the cadence is
enforced on this machine rather than depending on memory. It detects captures from the
artifact itself — newest `*_baylor.csv` in `~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/data/weekly_snapshots/`
— matching the script's existing "the artifact is the record, not a state file" rule.

**The real deadline is Saturday's kickoffs, not a maintenance window.** The report
overwrites its Chance of Victory column with the realised result once a game is *played* —
that is what destroyed 2019–2025. Nothing scheduled updates midweek.

Cadence (Monday-anchored, per Eric 2026-08-15 — he wanted the warning early in the week):
**Mon DUE → Tue–Sat OVERDUE → Sun silent** (games played, week gone). Season bounds are the
Monday of the opening week (2026-08-24) and the Saturday of the closing week (2027-01-23),
