4:  Health-check Eric's automation/memory stack in one pass and verify the Mac-to-Windows
5:  handoff works: launchd agents / Windows scheduled tasks, Python venvs, memsearch, the memory-compiler flush
20:/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/.claude/skills/claude-stack-doctor/scripts/stack-check.ps1   # Mac
21:pwsh -NoProfile -File $HOME\.claude\skills\claude-stack-doctor\scripts\stack-check.ps1                 # Windows
24:The same script runs on both machines and picks its checks by OS (see **Two machines** below). On Windows use `pwsh` 7, not `powershell` 5.1, which reports false `memsearch-run` / `backup-cloud-check` failures.
28:## Cross-machine handoff (runs on BOTH machines)
36:It answers a question nothing else here asked: did state actually make the trip between the two machines? Every other check verifies a component. This verifies the path.
38:The failure it exists to catch: `daily-backup` pushes `global-memory` nightly and, until 2026-09-12, nothing on the receiving machine ever pulled it. The Windows laptop was found 4 commits behind with every other signal reading healthy, because the backup section measures `ahead` only — which catches a broken push and is blind to a missing pull.
42:- `handoff-memory-stale` — `global-memory` is behind origin. This is the serious one: memory written on the other machine is on GitHub and not here, so this session is running on stale context. Fix with `/startup`, or `git -C ~/.claude/global-memory pull --no-rebase`.
44:- `handoff-unpushed:<repo>` — this machine is more than 3 commits ahead. The other machine cannot see this work; run `/closeout`.
47:- A repo absent from the machine entirely is skipped, not failed. `SecondBrain` is Mac-only and its absence on Windows is correct.
49:The "memory flow" line reports how long since `origin/main` on `global-memory` last advanced. Over 14 days it says so without failing: it cannot distinguish "quiet fortnight" from "the other machine's backup stopped pushing", and a check that cries wolf during the first gets ignored during the second.
51:## Two machines
53:`stack-check.ps1` tests `$env:OS -eq 'Windows_NT'` and swaps the machine-specific sections. Everything else (memsearch, flush pipeline, memory repos, cloud receipt, context budget, handoff) is shared.
55:| Section | Mac | Windows laptop |
57:| Jobs | launchd `com.keystone.*` agents | Task Scheduler: `Backup AI Sessions to Drive`, `DailyGmailDigest`, `CFB-ForecastCaptureReminder` (disabled tasks are skipped) |
61:| SecondBrain | checked | skipped, it is Mac-only |
63:Windows issue codes:
66:- `task-dual-run:<name>`: a `KeystoneOS-*` task is enabled on Windows. The Mac owns those jobs and the data pulls; disable the Windows copy.
70:On the Windows laptop the weekly run is Task Scheduler task `\Eric\KeystoneOS-StackDoctor` (Mondays 10:30, pwsh 7). It is the one `KeystoneOS-*` task that stays enabled on Windows.
72:**Mac notes.** Jobs are **launchd user agents** in `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`. The script is PowerShell because `pwsh` runs it natively on both machines. PowerShell on macOS normalises `\` inside a path string to `/`, so the script's mixed separators resolve correctly — verified 2026-08-29. Do not "fix" them.
74:Useful launchd commands:
77:launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.<name>                  # live schedule and state
78:launchctl bootout  gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.<name>               # unload
79:launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.<name>.plist   # reload
85:launchd agent `com.keystone.stackdoctor` (Mondays 10:30) runs `scripts/weekly-check.ps1`: the same read-only check, unattended. On failure it appends a one-line summary to `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` (surfaced at every session start per CLAUDE.md) and the full output is always in `scripts/last-weekly-run.log`. When a session surfaces such an entry, run this skill interactively to diagnose and fix, then clear the entry from `.errors.log`.
87:**Clearing `.errors.log`:** shell truncation (`: > file`) anywhere under `$HOME` is blocked by dcg rule `core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`. Use `cp /dev/null <file>`. There is no `truncate` binary on this machine. Archive first — the lines are often live issues, not stale history:
97:### `task:*` / `task-stale:*` — launchd agent failed or didn't run
98:1. Read the `action:` line the script printed and run that exact command **manually in a foreground terminal** — launchd discards stdout unless the plist sets `StandardOutPath`; foreground shows the real error.
99:2. Known root causes: executable referenced without a full path (launchd agents get a minimal PATH — always use full paths like `/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh`, and set `EnvironmentVariables:PATH` in the plist); a plist edited but never `bootout`+`bootstrap`ed, so the old schedule is still live; the job firing at an hour the required volume is unmounted (see `backup-*`).
104:macOS root causes: a Homebrew `python3` major-version bump orphans venvs built against the old interpreter; a `uv` reinstall or relocation breaks tools that hardcode `/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv` (CLAUDE.md forbids relocating it for this reason).
106:*History (Windows box, retired 2026-08-14): Python Install Manager migrations deleted `C:\Python31x` twice, silently killing morning-briefing for 6 days. The lesson transfers — an interpreter move breaks every venv built on it — the paths do not.*
109:memsearch is a **uv tool** on this machine: binary at `/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/memsearch`, environment at `/Users/kristinarash/.local/share/uv/tools/memsearch/`.
130:launchd agent `com.keystone.dailybackup` (**09:00 daily** since 2026-08-29) runs `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1`: auto-commits+pushes the memory repos (SecondBrain, dotclaude, claude-skills, claude-global-memory), **rsync**-snapshots `~/.claude/projects`, `~/.codex`, `~/.gemini` and non-repo DEV folders to Google Drive at `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/…`, captures the same set to the **CRASHBOX SSD** at `/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/` when it is mounted, runs an uncapped full memsearch reindex, and resets the hook's timeout-streak counter. Restore procedure: `~/.claude/RESTORE.md`.
136:- `backup-cloud-*` → the Drive-API heartbeat (gws CLI queries RESTORE.md's cloud modifiedTime). `-check` = gws auth rot; re-auth needs explicit full scope URLs: `gws auth login --scopes "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly"` (the `-s drive` shorthand silently grants NO scopes, v0.22.5 bug). After re-auth delete `~/.config/gws/token_cache.json` or it serves the stale token. The login is interactive — Eric must run it himself via `!` while at the machine, then open the printed URL directly; terminal copy/paste truncates it at line-wrap. `-stale`/`-missing` = files reach the local CloudStorage cache but Google Drive for Desktop isn't syncing — check that Google Drive is running and signed in.
148:- **Desktop Commander MCP times out at session start on Windows.** It starts through `npx -y …@latest`, which checks the npm registry every time: 23s alone, 30–46s alongside the other servers, against a 30s default. `MCP_TIMEOUT=90000` in `~/.claude/settings.json` `env` fixes it (set 2026-09-22). If it times out again, raise the timeout; don't edit the synced plugin's `plugin.json`, which is re-synced on the next launch.

# Handoff — 2026-09-21 — The Mac owns the GPS, Perch and VALD pulls

## What and why

The session started with a Mac `/dev-sync`. Eric then made the Mac the one machine that pulls the three
athlete data feeds: Catapult GPS, Perch (1RM) and VALD ForceDecks (CMJ + IMTP). Before this, Perch was
decided as Windows-owned (09-20), VALD had no working pull anywhere since 2026-08-02, and GPS ran on the
Mac at 06:30 and failed when the Mac slept.

## Decisions (with the reasoning)

- **All three pulls live on the Mac.** Eric briefly chose Windows for GPS, then reversed the same
  afternoon. One writer per database: two gitignored caches drift apart without any conflict warning.
- **Pull times moved to business hours:** GPS 10:00 + 16:30, Perch 10:05 + 16:35, VALD 10:10 + 16:40.
  The Mac is awake then, so the `pmset` wake question is dropped. The jobs are 5 minutes apart so they
  do not overlap.
- **Perch was refilled from the API, not copied from Windows.** `perch_ingest.py` upserts by
  athlete/exercise/date, and each run re-derives from the API, so the Windows copy was not needed.
  Result: 13,436 rows through 2026-09-21, more than the Windows copy (13,346 on 09-19).
- **Scheduled runs pull a short window:** Perch = the last 14 days from the newest stored test_date. VALD =
  from 3 days before the last successful run (the VALD API filters by `modifiedFromUtc`).
- **Token and secret rotation skipped for now** (Catapult token, VALD client secret). Eric's call; the
  repos are private and the pulls work.

## Root cause of the VALD failure

`src/ingest/pipeline.py` had `client: "VALDClient" | None`. Python evaluates that at import time and
raises TypeError before 3.14, so every entry point crashed on import. Fixed by quoting the whole hint.
Separately, the Windows `.bat` called `pipeline.py`, which has no entry point; the real one is
`run_pipeline.py`.

## Files created or modified

- `~/DEV/DataBase_GPS_Reporting/ops/com.keystone.gpspull.plist` (times), `gps_report/pull.sh` (comment),
  `docs/STATUS.md`
- `~/DEV/PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026/pull_perch.sh` (new), `ops/com.keystone.perchpull.plist` (new),
  `.gitignore`, `docs/STATUS.md`; `.venv/` (new, uv); `data/backups/perch_pre-backfill_2026-09-21.duckdb`
- `~/DEV/ForcePlate_DecisionSystem/src/ingest/pipeline.py` (fix), `pull_vald.sh` (new),
  `ops/com.keystone.valdpull.plist` (new), `.gitignore`, `docs/STATUS.md`; `.venv/` (new, uv);
  `data/backups/forceplate_pre-mac-pull_2026-09-21.db`
- `~/DEV/_INBOX/refresh_all_data.bat` (step 1 REM'd; step 3 was REM'd by the Windows session in PR #3,
  merged), `docs/STATUS.md`
- `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.{gpspull,perchpull,valdpull}.plist` (installed and loaded)
- `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (GPS and VALD+Perch lines),
  `transcripts/2026-09-19.md` and `2026-09-21.md` (merge conflicts resolved by keeping both sides)
- Drive: `02_SPORTS/Football/FA2026/_Mark_for_Deletion/gps_db_handoff_2026-09-21/` (the unused GPS DB
  copy, safe to delete)

## First scheduled afternoon runs (2026-09-21) — all passed, two ran late

- GPS 16:32: ok, exit 0, no new sessions (DB newest 2026-09-19).
- Perch and VALD: the Mac idle-slept at 15:45, so both started at 16:45:33 on a wake and then crept
  through DarkWakes (brief background wakes with no usable network). VALD finished ok at 17:36. Perch
  hit two read timeouts and passed on attempt 3 at 17:39 (DB newest 2026-09-21). No alerts fired.
- Open for Eric: `sudo pmset repeat wakeorpoweron MTWRFSU 16:28:00` to wake the Mac for the afternoon
  runs (recommended), or leave it and accept late runs. Morning runs at 10:00 usually find it awake.

## Next actions

1. Eric decides on the 16:28 wake (above). Then check the 2026-09-22 receipts: each `logs/last_run.json`
   should say `"status": "ok"` (GPS: `DataBase_GPS_Reporting/gps_report/logs/`; Perch:
   `PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026/logs/`; VALD: `ForcePlate_DecisionSystem/logs/`).
2. The Perch and VALD failure alerts have not fired yet. Treat the first real failure as the test.
3. Optional: add scipy to ForcePlate requirements (`tests/test_heterogeneity.py` needs it).
4. Optional: have `claude-stack-doctor` read the three receipts.

## Gotchas

- VALD pipeline stdout prints athlete names in `FLAG:` lines. Filter them out of anything that reaches
  chat or a transcript. `logs/` is gitignored in both new repos.
====INBOX
  - `perch.duckdb` last written **2026-09-19 11:47:54 AM**, created 2026-04-25. It holds **13,346 rows** (April's ingest left 12,300) with `max(test_date) = 2026-09-18`. That is real new data, not a touched mtime.
  - **It cannot have arrived by git.** The file is untracked and gitignored (`.gitignore:18 *.duckdb`), `dev-sync` moves work through GitHub only and never transports ignored files, and the repo's last fetch was 2026-09-18 — a day *before* the write. A file-level sync (Drive for desktop is still an open question below) is argued against separately: **only this one gitignored file moved** — `.env`, `__pycache__` and the rest still date from March/April, which is not what a bulk copy looks like.
  - So **Windows is an active Perch writer.** The credential lives in `PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026/.env` (present since April), `src/perch_ingest.py` runs against the live API, and step 3 of `refresh_all_data.bat` is still enabled — only the GPS step was REM'd.
  - The 11:47 AM write was **not** the scheduled run: `\Refresh_All_Data` last ran 2026-09-19 **8:45:50 PM** and returned `2147946720` (`0x800710E0`, the same non-zero code `DailyGmailDigest` returns — the sleep/power signature, cf. the DailyBackup note). The task has a single daily 8:00 PM trigger, no repetition, `StartWhenAvailable=False`, `StopIfGoingOnBatteries=True`. So the 09-19 morning write was an **ad-hoc run by hand**, most likely the "run the `.bat` once by hand" step listed under Next.
  - **Still unverified from this box: whether the Mac also writes Perch.** No Perch launchd plist exists in any repo here (only `com.keystone.gpspull.plist`, which is GPS), so there is no evidence of a Mac-side Perch job in version control — but the Mac keeps its own gitignored copy of `perch.duckdb`, so two independent caches can drift without either machine ever seeing a conflict. That is the GPS failure shape, and it is the half of the question that needs the Mac to answer.

## Next

  on merge). Hand-run of the edited `.bat`: Perch skipped, exit 0. The 20:00 run before the merge still
  pulls Perch into the Windows cache: API calls, not data. Windows GPS pull check the same day: no
  Windows task has run GPS since 09-09; `\Refresh_All_Data` is the only data task.
  VALD (`forceplate.db`, step 1): still to build on the Mac; keep Windows step 1 until then. It is broken
  anyway (`No module named 'src'`; entry point is `run_pipeline.py` from the repo root; needs
  `VALD_CLIENT_ID`, `VALD_CLIENT_SECRET`, `VALD_REGION_URL`, `VALD_TEAM_ID`), so Windows writes nothing
  meanwhile. **Done 2026-09-21:** the Mac job `com.keystone.valdpull` is live (10:10 + 16:40,
  `forceplate.db` current to 2026-09-21) and step 1 is REM'd in the `.bat` on main.
- **2026-09-21: Windows task `\Refresh_All_Data` DISABLED** (Eric, elevated PowerShell; confirmed
  `State: Disabled`). All three `.bat` steps were already REM'd, so it had nothing left to run. Windows now
  runs no data pulls; GPS, Perch and VALD live only on the Mac. Do not re-enable it. Changing this task
  needs admin: `Disable-ScheduledTask`/`schtasks /Change` return Access denied from a normal shell.
- Gotcha found 2026-09-21: Google Drive for Desktop backs up the whole `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV`
  folder (Drive root "DEV"; 3.1 GB in `DEV\.tmp.driveupload`). Every DuckDB in DEV on Windows sits under
  it. Harmless so far, but it contradicts "DuckDB stays local" and may be what holds files open when git
  cannot delete worktree folders. Eric's call whether to keep it.
- Rotate the exposed VALD client secret. Do not print or reuse the historical value; after rotation, verify the replacement is stored outside Git and project documentation.

**Resolved 2026-08-11.** Recording the trap because the error message points the wrong way.

`fireflies-pp-cli` failed on **every** command and every `--data-source` (including
`live`) with:

```
Error: querying: unable to open database file: out of memory (14)
```

"Out of memory" is wrong — SQLite 14 is `SQLITE_CANTOPEN`. The real cause: the local
mirror had **never been created on this Mac**. Two things were missing after the
Windows → Mac migration:

1. No `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` anywhere — not env, not disk, not Keychain.
2. No database. `sync` had never been run here.

I sent the calling agent the full inventory. The Mac runs about 15 launchd jobs, owns the athlete data pulls, and is the only machine meant to run the CFB forecast capture. The job list comes from synced notes and the stack-doctor script; none of it can be checked live from Windows. I changed no files.

**Scheduled jobs on the Mac**
- **Backup:** `com.keystone.dailybackup` runs at 09:00. It pushes SecondBrain, dotclaude, skills and global-memory, copies to Drive and to the CRASHBOX SSD when it's plugged in, and reindexes memsearch. It won't run on Windows, which uses its own `Backup AI Sessions to Drive` robocopy task instead.
- **KeystoneOS jobs:** `reconcile` (07:00 and at login), `morning` (weekdays 06:00), `rituals` (weekdays 17:00, Fri 15:30), `agysync` (every 6 hours), `adjudicate` (Sun 02:30), `aiosaudit` (1st of the month, 14:00) and `commandcentre` (the always-on page at localhost:7373). None of these has a live Windows copy; the Windows versions have been disabled since 08-14.
- **Stack doctor** is the one job that runs on both machines, Mondays at 10:30.
- **Data pulls:** GPS at 10:00 and 16:30, Perch at 10:05 and 16:35, VALD at 10:10 and 16:40. The matching steps in the Windows `refresh_all_data.bat` are commented out, and the `\Refresh_All_Data` task was disabled on 09-21.
- **Probably stale:** `graphextract` (09:30 daily; its own doc says to remove it when done) and two Life-OS OneDrive sync jobs at 02:00. I can't tell whether they are still loaded.

**Ownership decisions**
- 08-14: all KeystoneOS jobs moved to the Mac.
- 09-13: the Mac owns the GPS database.
- 09-21: the Mac owns the GPS, Perch and VALD pulls; Windows writes none of them. This reversed the 09-20 decision that Windows owned Perch.
- 09-23: the Mac owns the weekly CFB forecast capture and it must never run on Windows. The Windows reminder task was disabled.

**Mac-only tools and data**
- The CRASHBOX SSD backups and the localhost:7373 status page.
- Secrets in the macOS Keychain, such as the Fireflies key.
- The Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) login, recorded in the Mac's notes.
- The main GPS, Perch and VALD databases, and the S2_Evaluation `data/` folder.
- Scripts with macOS-only code, such as `skill-button.sh`, which hardcodes Mac paths.

Two things the docs call Mac-only are also on this laptop:
- The custom `~/go/bin` command-line tools are installed here as `.exe` files.
- SecondBrain was restored at `Desktop\SecondBrain` on 09-17, though stack doctor still skips it on Windows.

**Only on Windows**
- Docker and Milvus for memsearch. The Mac removed Docker on 09-03.
- The `Backup AI Sessions to Drive` and `DailyGmailDigest` tasks.
- Google Drive mirroring the whole DEV folder. The Mac stopped doing this on 08-14.
- The PFF database belongs to neither machine: each keeps its own copy and they swap Parquet files through Drive.

**Open questions**
- No note confirms from the Mac that the Windows GPS writer has actually stopped.
- The CFB capture has no schedule on either machine; a reminder prompts a manual run. The notes also disagree on the day: memory says Monday, the project status file says the next run is Wednesday 09-30.
- The KeystoneOS job registry lists only 3 jobs, not the full set.
- The Catapult token and VALD secret haven't been rotated (your call on 09-21).
- Windows still has no restore runbook.

The key sources are `.claude\skills\claude-stack-doctor\SKILL.md`, `.claude\global-memory\handoffs\2026-09-21-mac-owns-data-pulls.md`, `Desktop\DEV\CFB_Victory_Model\docs\STATUS.md` and `Desktop\DEV\_INBOX\docs\STATUS.md`.
